items.explanation: 71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5, coded 42731 at the 2025-08-22 admission) and no anticoagulant at any point in the chart: every cardiology clinic note from 2025-10-10 through 2026-07-28 lists only tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, and no warfarin/DOAC order is active on 2026-09-24. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), for which the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation (score >=2 in men). Needs review for starting anticoagulation; note the 2025 procedural hemorrhage diagnosis when weighing bleeding risk.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (MedicationRequest c17946a1, ambulatory CMED encounter 67ac34da; it does not appear on any earlier medication list). Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, 5 days after the start, so the requirement is completed (that ECG showed sinus rhythm with QTc 373 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (MedicationRequest cbe91d0f, ambulatory CMED encounter d08380fb). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (the revised memo explicitly leaves earlier starts on 30 days): ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - within the required time, so completed (QTc about 488 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started as an outpatient at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (MedicationRequest e578297f, ambulatory CMED encounter d3b727df; the note of 2025-08-02 did not list amiodarone, the 2025-11-10 note does). Start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 30 days, by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start - completed. (That ECG showed QTc 522 ms, which is itself flagged separately for prescriber review.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (MedicationRequest 4dde586a, ambulatory CMED encounter 2320ecfd; it is new on that visit's medication list compared with 2026-06-24). Start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - due 2026-08-15. No ECG has been obtained since: her only tracing is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, and no ECG or ECG report appears in the chart after the escitalopram start, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was ordered at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (MedicationRequest 88943096, ambulatory CMED encounter 8fe73d19) - the first escitalopram order in the chart. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised 14-day window applies, so an ECG was due by 2026-04-24. The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start, i.e. outside the required 14-day window, so the monitoring requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue. (The late tracing showed sinus rhythm, QTc 375 ms, with probable limb-lead reversal.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (MedicationRequest f757652a, ambulatory CMED encounter 3c630899; not on the 2026-02-27 medication list). Start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - due 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference 5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (MedicationRequest 9db19264, ambulatory CMED encounter 02750626; haloperidol is new on that note's medication list). Start is after 3/1/2026 so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been done since the start (last tracing 104253928 from 2025-03-09), but the window is still open as of the 2026-09-24 review - not yet due; the ECG should be arranged before 9/29.

Cardiology Clinic clinician note of 2026-09-01 (DocumentReference b32487e8, Dr. Kessler) documents 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician after the 3/1/2026 effective date, so an INR was required within 7 days (due 2026-09-08). INR(PT) 2.3 was drawn on 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the change, so the requirement is completed.

Anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 2026-09-10 (DocumentReference 9579a764, L. Nguyen PharmD) documents 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the standing order, so a follow-up INR was required within 7 days (due 2026-09-17). No INR has been resulted since: the most recent INR(PT) in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change. The INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old on warfarin plus amiodarone.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300, I48.0, recorded 2025-03-14) who is on no anticoagulant: cardiology clinic notes from 2025-04-24 through 2026-07-10 list only metoprolol, carvedilol and famotidine, and no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (her 2025-03-14 ECG 102298909 shows sinus rhythm with a PVC, consistent with paroxysmal AF). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior embolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia = 2 points, female sex), so guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is clearly indicated (class 1). Needs prescriber review; thrombocytopenia and falls history should be factored into the decision.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is a current order (MedicationRequest dc397aff, written 2026-08-20, valid to 2026-12-28) even though the outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 (DocumentReference 8fcbd349) documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with hemoglobin nadir 6.9 and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The 2026-08-20 clinic note nonetheless lists apixaban (plus aspirin and clopidogrel) and says continue current regimen, so the drug that was stopped for major bleeding has been restarted/continued without the documented cardiology review. Needs review of whether anticoagulation (and concomitant dual antiplatelet therapy) should continue.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (MedicationRequest 7206d5b5, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (MedicationRequest b71a461f, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note (DocumentReference a80a007c) states the anticoagulant is being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starts apixaban, but the rivaroxaban prescription was never discontinued and both remain valid on 2026-09-24 (the note's own medication list shows both). High bleeding risk - the rivaroxaban order should be cancelled.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 (DocumentReference 96cdf346) states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (15:08) and 103088543 (19:36) show atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.35-0.72 s, RMSSD 98-115 ms) with no organised P waves - at mean ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm. The documented rhythm and rate are both wrong, which matters because it is the basis for continuing her current management; the note should be corrected and the rapid AF addressed.

Patient is taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order MedicationRequest 8de890c6, 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02, continuously refilled since it was started 2024-05-14). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 476 ms at RR 0.88 s, i.e. QTc (Bazett) 508 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Note the 2024-05-14 clinic note described this same tracing as 'QT acceptable' when escitalopram was started. Most recent electrolytes are normal (K 4.1 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL, both 2025-08-23); no ECG has been repeated since.

79-year-old man on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order MedicationRequest 1014aca9, 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05; on amiodarone continuously since 2025-11-10) and warfarin. His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 514 ms at RR 0.97 s, QTc (Bazett) 522 ms - above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review, and up from QTc 427 ms on the previous tracing. Most recent electrolytes normal (K 4.4 mEq/L, Mg 2.2 mg/dL, both 2026-04-20). Review amiodarone dose/continuation and repeat the ECG.

Patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order MedicationRequest 7f787d30, 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25, refilled continuously at 40 mg since 2023-10-02; 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg/day ceiling usually advised for QT safety). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 482 ms at RR 0.86 s, QTc (Bazett) 521 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold (previous tracing QTc 424 ms). Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are needed.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order MedicationRequest c6f532e9, 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05; on amiodarone since 2022) plus warfarin and metoprolol. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a very long T wave: QT 546 ms at RR 1.04 s, QTc (Bazett) 534 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review (and up from 446 ms three weeks earlier). Most recent electrolytes: K 4.1 mEq/L and Mg 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14) - magnesium at the low end. Review amiodarone and obtain a current ECG.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular, PR 176 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 370 ms at RR 0.81 s (QTc 411 ms), axis about +65 deg. High-frequency artefact is present throughout but the spikes are not time-locked to the QRS and there is no evidence of pacing. No prior ECG in the chart.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm: RR constant at 0.54 s and every beat is preceded by a discrete upright P wave in II (negative in V1) with PR about 170 ms - beat-by-beat review shows one P per QRS and no flutter waves. QRS 88 ms with deep S in V1-V2 and tall R in V5-V6 (voltage criteria for LVH) but no bundle branch block; QT 290 ms (QTc 395 ms); axis about +36 deg. Prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was identical (115 bpm, QTc 384 ms) - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one premature beat and compensatory pause (RR 0.96-0.99 s otherwise, single 0.56 s coupling followed by 1.36 s), P wave with PR 192 ms before each sinus beat; QRS 96 ms; QT 384 ms (QTc 390 ms). Net QRS positive in I with negative II/III/aVF and mean frontal axis about -37 deg: left axis deviation. No bundle branch block (QRS <120 ms). Only ECG in the chart.

Regular rhythm at 70 bpm with a consistent atrial wave before each QRS (PR 136 ms) - sinus rhythm. QRS 88 ms, QT 348 ms (QTc 375 ms). All of I, II and aVL are deeply negative with a dominant positive complex in aVR, giving a mean frontal axis of about -170 deg (extreme/indeterminate); the normal R-wave progression in V4-V6 suggests limb-lead reversal rather than true dextrocardia, and this should be confirmed on a repeat tracing. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 94 ms. Long flat T wave ending about 450 ms after QRS onset: QT 482 ms at RR 0.86 s, QTc (Bazett) 521 ms - prolonged (patient on citalopram 40 mg). Axis about +50 deg, no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) had QTc 424 ms, an increase of about 95 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 80 ms. The T wave is inverted/biphasic in I, V2-V6 with a late return to baseline at about 400-430 ms after QRS onset: QT approximately 458 ms at RR 0.88 s, QTc (Bazett) approximately 488 ms - borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold. Axis about +39 deg, no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, PR 166 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 372 ms at RR 1.13 s (QTc 349 ms), axis about -15 deg, no conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) sinus at 66 bpm with QTc 387 ms - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS 84 ms. T wave is broad and late with terminal T at about 450 ms after QRS onset: QT 476 ms at RR 0.88 s, QTc (Bazett) 508 ms - markedly prolonged. Axis about +40 deg, no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) had QTc 361 ms, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 0.40-0.46 s, RMSSD 11 ms) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection preceding each QRS (PR about 170 ms) and no fibrillatory baseline - organised sinus tachycardia. QRS 80 ms; the T wave peaks about 185 ms after the QRS and ends by about 215 ms, giving QT approximately 260 ms at RR 0.43 s (QTc approximately 405 ms). Axis about -8 deg. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (RR 0.38-0.82 s, no P waves, QTc 423 ms), so the atrial fibrillation has resolved; QTc change less than 60 ms.
Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular, PR 132 ms, QRS 96 ms (no bundle branch block pattern), QT 362 ms at RR 0.73 s (QTc 424 ms), axis about +32 deg. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular, PR 162 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 334 ms (QTc 411 ms). Lead I is net positive while II, III and aVF are net negative by area (mean frontal axis about -50 deg): left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) sinus at 87 bpm, QTc 391 ms - no rhythm, block or QTc change.

Mean frontal axis about -27 deg (borderline, within normal range). Prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) showed the same LBBB with PR 210 ms and QTc 457 ms - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, regular, PR 138 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 328 ms (QTc 427 ms), axis about +48 deg, no conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 101016166 (2025-03-18) identical (102 bpm, QTc 421 ms) - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, regular, PR 152 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 370 ms at RR 0.91 s (QTc 387 ms). Net QRS positive in I with negative II and aVF (mean frontal axis about -31 deg): left axis deviation. QRS duration is normal so no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a P wave before each QRS (PR 182 ms); QRS 86 ms. Very long broad T wave ending about 500 ms after QRS onset: QT 546 ms at RR 1.04 s, QTc (Bazett) 534 ms - markedly prolonged (patient on amiodarone). Axis about +38 deg. The prior ECG 100867733 (2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation at about 131 bpm with QTc 446 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has risen by about 90 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, regular, PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT 304 ms (QTc 406 ms), axis about +47 deg, no conduction abnormality. Prior ECG 107274479 (2019-07-27) sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 413 ms - no change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, P wave before each QRS with PR 164 ms; QRS 86 ms, QT 430 ms at RR 1.16 s (QTc 399 ms); axis about +38 deg; tall precordial voltage but no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 104629882 (2023-05-22) sinus at 58 bpm with one premature beat, QTc 399 ms - no change.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm (RR 0.49 s) with small but consistent P waves, PR about 125 ms; QRS now narrow at 88 ms, QT 292 ms (QTc 415 ms). Frontal QRS forces are small with negative lead I and near-isoelectric aVF (net area slightly negative), i.e. an indeterminate/extreme axis. Compared with ECG 106516875 from earlier the same day, which showed QRS 148 ms with an rSR' and terminal R in V1 and wide S in I/V6 (RBBB), the QRS has normalised - resolved bundle branch block. QTc change (463 to 415 ms) is less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 94 ms. Long broad T wave: QT 514 ms at RR 0.97 s, QTc (Bazett) 522 ms - prolonged (patient on amiodarone). Axis about +67 deg, no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 108780865 (2025-06-07) had QTc 427 ms, an increase of about 95 ms.

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.38-1.10 s, RMSSD 270 ms) with no organised P waves (fibrillatory baseline, PQ-segment correlation between beats only 0.5) - no measurable PR interval. Mean ventricular rate about 97 bpm. QRS 78 ms, QT 324 ms (QTc 411 ms). Net QRS positive in I and negative in II/aVF: left axis deviation (about -65 deg). Only ECG in the chart.
